pages.text: "Mom, someone is coming." Pipo hid behind Mom and looked over the wall. Mrs. Badger walked along it with a cloth bundle. Mom whispered, "Our new neighbor."
Mrs. Badger waved from beyond the wall. "Hello! You must be Pipo!" He wanted to wave and make friends. But his hands only gripped the scarf, and he hid farther behind Mom.
Smiling, she walked away along the wall. Pipo peeped over it, pouting at not greeting her. "...I wanted to too."
Mom stood Pipo before the wall. "Say hello across the wall, and the person there becomes a neighbor." He repeated softly, "Say hello, make a neighbor!"
Mom met the sheep's eyes beyond the wall and smiled. "Hello!" They answered baa. Pipo laughed and practiced with them. "Hello... hello!"
Near evening, Mrs. Badger returned with her bundle. Pipo breathed out deeply. One step toward the wall, then another. Behind him, Mom gave a thumbs-up.
Both hands on the wall, Pipo looked into her eyes. "Hello!" His small, clear voice crossed the wall. She stopped and smiled widely. "Hello, Pipo!"
She opened the bundle on the wall. Out came a round cheese. "Now we are neighbors, let us share." She broke off half for him. Pipo crouched, hands at his chest.
Now greetings came easily. "One, go to the wall! Two, eyes meet and smile! Three, hello!" The next morning, when she passed, he raised one hand high. "Hello!"
Mom hugged his shoulders. "Hello brought you a neighbor, right?" One hello made an unfamiliar neighbor their neighbor. Pipo called bravely, "Say hello, make a neighbor!"
